headline: Economy stalls, tariffs linger and the U.S. heads to the polls
summary: Canada's economy stalled just as the Bank of Canada raised rates, and trade talks with Washington continued without a deal. The Iran conflict kept energy prices high, and Ontario's deficit grew. The week ended with the U.S. midterms about to begin and Ottawa's budget days away.

top.headline: Carney reports 'good conversation' with Trump as trade teams keep talking
top.what: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he had a good call with Donald Trump on a possible trade deal, with officials working over the coming weeks, but U.S. tariffs remain in place.
top.why: Tariffs affect Ontario's auto, steel and manufacturing jobs.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: Statistics Canada says the economy was flat in August and probably shrank 0.1% in September, a weak backdrop for the Bank of Canada's first rate increase since 2023.
top.why: Higher borrowing costs and a stalled economy squeeze mortgages and jobs.

top.headline: Trump says Iran war will end 'one way or the other' as Hormuz plan waits
top.what: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the U.S. meets its conditions, keeping oil and fuel prices elevated.
top.why: Energy prices feed directly into gas and heating costs in Ontario.

top.headline: U.S. midterms arrive Tuesday; administration takes California ballot fight to Supreme Court
top.what: Over 53 million Americans voted early, polls point to a tight race, and the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court on Monday to sideline about 20,000 disputed California mail ballots.
top.why: Control of Congress shapes U.S. tariff and trade policy toward Canada.

top.headline: Ontario's deficit swells to $16.9 billion as tariffs delay balanced budget
top.what: The province's fall economic statement pushes a balanced budget out to 2029-30.
top.why: Affects provincial spending on health, transit and services.

top.headline: Police chief defends response after Bridle Path suspect was let go from hospital
top.what: A Canada-wide warrant is out for a 23-year-old suspect and two others are sought after the violent Oct. 29 home invasion.
top.why: Home invasions in Toronto are up about 32% this year, per police.

top.headline: Federal budget lands Thursday with a focus on small-business tax relief
top.what: Finance Minister Champagne will table the budget on Nov. 5, previewing tax-complexity relief for small businesses.
top.why: The budget sets Ottawa's response to tariffs and a stalling economy.

top.headline: Kherson truce ends as Russian strikes leave Ukrainians without power
top.what: A short humanitarian ceasefire around Oleshky ended Sunday while strikes on Ukraine's grid continued; talks are hoped for Nov. 6–10 in Abu Dhabi.
top.why: Shapes energy markets and Canada's aid commitments.
